2. The defendant was earlier a partner in a franchisee firm that operated a Frankfinn centre at Satara, Maharashtra, but the franchise arrangement failed due to non-performance and internal disputes among the partners.

The plaintiff alleges that on 18.06.2015, the defendant misused police machinery by bringing police officials from Satara to the plaintiff's Janakpuri office, unlawfully detaining one of the plaintiff's officials for nearly ten hours, and coercing the plaintiff into an illegal settlement under threat of arrest.

sentences.text: The plaintiff further alleges that the defendant misrepresented his status as a partner and had earlier lodged FIR No. 09/2014 at Satara without the plaintiff's knowledge, despite the partnership firm having ceased to exist and co-partners having already taken action against the defendant.

Upon discovering the fraud and misuse of police power, the plaintiff refused to act upon the coerced settlement, sought return of the cash and cheques, and issued stop-payment instructions to its bank.

The defendant allegedly failed to return the money and cheques and left the plaintiff's office,
confirming misuse of police authority and fraudulent conduct.

sentences.text: 5. The plaintiff also alleges that the defendant has repeatedly defamed it by making false allegations of fraud and cheating through electronic media, particularly by publishing a complaint titled "Fraud played upon us by Director of Frankfinn" on Zee 24 Taas and related online platforms.

The plaintiff contends that these defamatory statements are false, malicious, and intended to damage its goodwill, resulting in loss of reputation, business humiliation, and inability to secure new franchisees, especially in Maharashtra.

6. It is asserted that the defendant's defamatory acts are continuous, have caused irreparable harm to the plaintiff's goodwill and business, and that such loss cannot be adequately quantified in monetary terms.
The plaintiff claims compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the tortious acts of defamation and Rs.1,00,000/- towards recovery of the coerced cash amount, along with interest.
7. The plaintiff submits that the cause of action arose on 18.06.2015 and continues thereafter, that the suit is within limitation, and that the Delhi Court has territorial jurisdiction.
The suit has been properly valued and requisite Court fees have been paid.

18. The plaintiff has examined PW1 Shri Kuldeep Singh who relied upon his affidavit and documents tendered by him in exparte evidence.
The plaintiff has also examined PW2 PW2 Shri Anant Arjun Chinchkar Retd. SI, Satara posted at Local Crime Branch, Satara in the year 2014.

19. The plaintiff alleges defendant misused police by getting registered FIR 09/2014 after dissolution of partnership and the police detained official of the plaintiff and coerced Rs.1,00,000/-
cash and 4 cheques of Rs.29,00,000/- via illegal settlement.
PW2 confirms lawful police inquiry as per Court order.
PW2 stated that he found that plaintiff official was an employee and there was financial business transaction between plaintiff and defendant and no criminal offence was made out.
Thereafter notice under Section 160 Cr.PC was given to Anshul Gaba Ex.PW1/7.
He admitted that Ex.PW1/4 and PW1/5 is in the handwriting of the defendant and bears signatures of the defendant.
The testimony of PW2 is nowhere mentions that the said documents were executed by use of any force or coercion by either of the parties.
PW2 also did not corroborate the version of PW1 regarding any illegal process.
Thus, the said documents were voluntarily executed by the defendant without any duress, threats or violence.
Further, the plaintiff unilaterally stopped chequesEx.PW1/8 and 10.
The defendant neither encashed nor retained the said cheques.
20. Hence, it is nowhere proved by the plaintiff that the cash amount of Rs. 1,00,000/- or the cheques were handed over due to any coercion.
